Meaning: *bāliyah* (worn away, decayed). It is also read *nākhirah*, from *nakhara al-ʿaẓm*, meaning the bone decayed, so that when the wind passes through it, a hollow sound (*nakhīr*) is heard from it.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[17–19] ﴿Go to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed.﴾ ﴿And say, "Is there for you an inclination to purify yourself?"﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 18] ﴿And I would guide you to your Lord, so you would fear Him.﴾ [An-Nazi'at: 19]

﴿Go to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed.﴾ That is: he became arrogant and exceeded his limit in aggression against the Children of Israel, and in claiming the attributes of lordship and attributing them to himself.

End.

[20–26] ﴿So he showed him the greatest sign﴾ ﴿but he denied and disobeyed﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 21] ﴿Then he turned his back, striving﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 22] ﴿Then he gathered [his people] and proclaimed﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 23] ﴿Saying, "I am your lord, the most high"﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 24] ﴿So God seized him, [as] an example for the Hereafter and the first [life]﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 25] ﴿Indeed, in that is a lesson for whoever fears﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 26]

The sense is: he went, conveyed the message, returned, and challenged him, and then he showed him the greatest sign. According to Mujahid, this was his staff and his hand: his staff when it turned into a manifest serpent, and his hand when he brought it out white for the onlookers. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 79, verses 27–33:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[27–33] ﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven? He constructed it.﴾ ﴿He raised its height and made it even.﴾ ﴿And He darkened its night and brought out its forenoon.﴾ ﴿And after that He spread the earth.﴾ ﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture.﴾ ﴿And the mountains He set firmly.﴾ ﴿As a provision for you and your livestock.﴾

﴿Are you more difficult to create, or is the heaven?﴾ This is an address to the deniers of the Resurrection among the Quraysh, whose statement was mentioned at the beginning of the surah, by way of rebuke, to alert them to how easy it is for the Lord's power. For He who raised the heaven in its greatness, creating them and creating their like, and reviving them after their death, is easy for Him.

As He, glorified is He, said: ﴿The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 57], and His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 81]. Then He explained the manner of its creation with His saying: ﴿He constructed it.﴾ Ibn Jarir said: that is, He raised it and made it a ceiling for the earth. Al-Imam said: construction (bina') is the joining of scattered parts to one another, together with binding them by what holds them, until a single structure results from them. This is what God did with the stars: He placed each of them in a relation to the others, along with what holds each in its orbit, until from them there resulted one visible sign, named by one name, which is the heaven above us. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿He raised its height﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 28], that is, its elevation. The "samk" (height) is the stature of everything, and He, exalted is He, raised its bodies above our heads. ﴿And made it even﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 28], that is, He balanced it by placing each body in its position.

﴿And He darkened its night﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 29], that is, He made it dark. Ibn Jarir said: He attributed the night to the heaven, because the night is the setting of the sun, and its setting and rising occur in it; so it was attributed to it because of what was in it, as it is said: "the stars of the night," since in it occur the rising and the setting.

﴿And brought out its forenoon﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 29], that is, He made its daylight manifest. The "duha" (forenoon) is the spreading of the sun and the extension of the day; and the choice of the forenoon is because it is the time when the sun's dominion is established and its brightness is complete.

"And after that He spread the earth" — that is, after the arranging of the heaven in the aforementioned manner, and the manifestation of the lights — "spread it" — that is, He extended it and made it level for the dwelling of its people and their movement across its regions.

﴿He extracted from it its water﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 31], that is, by making springs gush forth from it and causing rivers to flow. ﴿And its pasture﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 31], that is, its grazing, which is vegetation.

Al-Shihab said: The "mar'a" (pasture) is what animals other than humans eat; so it is intended here, metaphorically, as the general sense of what is eaten by humans and others; thus it is a figurative metonymy (majaz mursal).

Al-Tibi said: It may be an explicit metaphor (isti'ara musarraha), because the address is with the deniers of the Gathering, as witnessed by His saying: ﴿Are you more difficult to create?﴾ It is as if it were said: O stubborn ones, bound by the horns of cattle, in enjoying the world and being heedless of the Hereafter.

﴿And the mountains He set firmly﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 32], that is, He fixed them in it.

﴿As a provision for you and your livestock﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 33], that is, for benefit for a time. Abu al-Su'ud said: its accusative case is either as an object of purpose (maf'ul lahu), meaning: He did that as provision for you and your livestock, since the benefit of what was mentioned of spreading and laying out, and the extraction of water and pasture, reaches them and their livestock; for what is meant by pasture encompasses what humans and others eat, as has preceded. Or it is an absolute infinitive (masdar) emphasizing its implied verb, meaning: He provided you with that as a provision; or it is a verbal noun not from its own verb, since His saying: ﴿He extracted from it its water and its pasture﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 31] carries the meaning of "provided with that."

The discussion of the saying of His Exalted Name:

﴿So when the Greatest Calamity comes﴾ — that is, the great catastrophe that overwhelms every terrifying matter, so that its immense terror submerges everything else; it is the Resurrection for reckoning and recompense.

﴿The Day when man will remember what he strove for﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 35] — that is, what he did of good or evil, by its being presented to him.

﴿And Hellfire will be brought forth for whoever sees﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 36] — that is, the Fire of God will be made manifest to the eyes of onlookers.

﴿As for he who transgressed﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 37] — that is, he who went to excess in his aggression and in exceeding the limit of the Sharia and the truth, to the commission of disobedience, corruption and error.

﴿And preferred the worldly life﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 38] — that is, its enjoyments and its desires, over the honour of the Hereafter and what has been prepared therein for the righteous.

﴿Then indeed Hellfire will be his refuge﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 39] — that is, his abode and his place of return. (p-6054)

﴿But as for he who feared the standing before his Lord﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 40] — that is, his standing before Him to be questioned, or His majesty and greatness; that is, he feared Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobediences; ﴿and restrained the soul from its desire﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 40] — that is, in what God dislikes and does not approve of from it, so he opposed it in favour of what He commanded him.

﴿Then indeed Paradise will be his refuge﴾ [an-Nazi'at: 41] — that is, his destination on the Day of Resurrection. The answer of (idha, "when") is omitted, because the division indicates it; its estimated meaning is: "the deeds will become manifest," or "the people will be divided into two groups."

**On the interpretation of His words, the Exalted:**

[42–46] ﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it come to rest?﴾ ﴿What have you to do with mentioning it?﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 43] ﴿To your Lord is its finality.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 44] ﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 45] ﴿On the day they see it, it will be as if they had not remained but an evening or a morning of it.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46]

﴿They ask you about the Hour: when will it come to rest?﴾ That is, its establishment (iqamatuha), meaning: when will Allah establish it and bring it into being?

Al-Nasir (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: In this there is an indication of the heaviness of that day, as in His words: ﴿And they leave behind them a heavy day.﴾ [al-Insan: 27] Do you not see that they use the word irsa' (anchoring) only for what has weight, such as the anchor of a ship and the anchoring of mountains?

﴿What have you to do with mentioning it?﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 43] That is: in what matter are you concerned with mentioning its hour to them? That is, mentioning it is not up to you, because it is among the unseen matters, so there is no point in their asking you about it.

For this reason He said: ﴿To your Lord is its finality.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 44] That is, the finality of its knowledge.

﴿You are only a warner to those who fear it.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 45] That is: you were sent only to warn those who fear its reckoning and Allah's punishment for their crimes. You were not charged with knowing the time of its establishment.

﴿On the day they see it, it will be as if they had not remained but an evening or a morning of it.﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 46] That is: these deniers of it, and of what it contains of recompense and reckoning, on the day they witness its occurrence, because of its tremendous terror, will feel that they had remained in the world, or in the graves, only an hour of a day, the length of an evening or a morning of it. The attribution of "morning" (duha) to "evening" (ashiyya) is because of the connection between them, since both belong to one day.
